bivariate_pairs.rationale: Variance and skewness both describe distribution shape; their relationship may reveal systematic patterns.
Variance and curtosis together capture spread and tail heaviness; checking interaction can uncover joint effects.
Skewness and curtosis jointly characterize asymmetry and peakedness; their interplay may be informative.
Entropy measures information content; relating it to variance can show how dispersion influences uncertainty.
Linking entropy with skewness may reveal whether asymmetric distributions carry more or less information.
